b: Triumph singer/guitarist Rik Emmett and Mojotone have collaborated on the Rock & Roll Machine, a versatile guitar preamp pedal that offers a broad array of distortion, overdriven, and boosted tones with the amplifier of your choice.

The Rock & Roll Machine uses Emmett’s searing signature sound from Triumph’s classic era as a starting point, with additional tone-shaping features such as a powerful three-band EQ section, ‘Oomph’ switch, and a Fat/Skinny knob for additional sonic sculpting.

The basis of Rock & Roll Machine’s British-flavored sound is Emmett’s customized 50-Watt plexi amplifiers from the late 1970s – the source of his bright, cutting tone from the early Triumph albums. The tone-shaping preamp approach, also informed by Emmett’s favorite studio EQs and recording chains, provides a versatile pedal for just about any music genre.

The pedal’s two footswitches operate in a unique fashion. The On/Off switch activates the pedal’s EQ tone shaping functions: Treble, Bass, Presence and Fat/Skinny knobs, as well as a two-position Oomph toggle switch. The pedal’s overdrive/distortion is only activated when you press the Boost footswitch, allowing you to control your overdriven tone with the Gain knob. The overdrive/distortion circuit is a mix of soft clipping and hard clipping, so it’s highly responsive to your right-hand attack and changes in your guitar’s volume knob setting.

“I want something more evolved than a typical distortion pedal – something that has warmth and depth to the sound without losing articulation,” Emmett explains. “The combination of those vintage Plexi amps and vintage Neve EQ channel strips provided me with that mix of cut and warmth, so I asked the designers at Mojotone to start there. The result is a preamp pedal with an incredibly articulate and responsive set of gain stages that can go from a clean boost, to crunch, to screaming lead, all with just the guitar’s volume knobs.”

Rock & Roll Machine’s rich, dynamic tones can be shaped from the onset with the pedal’s 3-Band EQ of Treble, Middle, and Bass Knobs. An additional Fat/Skinny knob can then be used to tune the overall body and character of the sound, adding additional warmth and thickness or cut and clarity as required. The Oomph switch offers two variations of low-end response for the pedal, and when activated evokes the punchy low-end of a closed 4x12 cabinet.
Treble, Bass, and Presence controls for easy, precise tone shaping
Fat/Skinny knob dials in warmth or cut
Oomph 2-position switch provides the tight bass of a closed-back 4x12 cabinet
Powered by 9-volt external DC supply – no battery compartment
